slides.title: Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion distribution and steady-state convergence times in multi-agent networks, providing insights for the societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion consensus time in networks using a 2k-choices majority rule.
card.key_idea: Identifies a phase transition where mixing time to steady-state is exponential (sub-critical), polynomial (critical), or logarithmic (super-critical) based on stubborn agent proportions.
card.evaluation: Theoretically derived scaling laws were numerically validated by solving forward Kolmogorov and detailed balance equations for mixing times.
card.limitation: The analysis is conducted on a fully connected network, which may not generalize to all network topologies.

slides.title: Mobility, Memory, and Network Structure in Agent-Based Models of Convention Tipping and Convergence
slides.highlight: This research on agent-based models of convention tipping and convergence is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: A study on how mobility, memory, and network structure determine the speed of social convention tipping.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model using a unified predictive equation to estimate convergence time based on committed-minority size, agent memory, influencer mobility, and network connectivity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 21,600 simulation samples across 432 configurations; the predictive model achieved R² = 0.91 and RMSE ≈ 57, outperforming simpler baselines.
card.limitation: A theoretical, stylized model that abstracts away cognitive and institutional richness, such as sanctions, values, or hierarchical authority.

slides.title: TRIBE: Predicting Team Performance via Communication Behavior Ensembles
slides.tldr: PREDICTING TEAM PERFORMANCE VIA COMMUNICATION PATTERNS
slides.highlight: TRIBE identifies behavioral tribes through communication patterns to predict team performance, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: TRIBE predicts team performance by clustering communication patterns, enabling behavioral interventions as early as 10% task-completion.
card.key_idea: A domain-independent pipeline using topic modeling (NMF/LDA) and clustering (GMM/k-means) to categorize teams into performance-predictive 'behavioral tribes' based on natural language transcripts.
card.evaluation: Tested on four diverse datasets (Minecraft, logical reasoning, survival ranking). Performance measured via adjusted R², ANOVA, and Cohen’s d; results show significant predictive power.
card.limitation: Effectiveness depends on task structure; tasks with limited behavioral freedom or small sample sizes reduce the model's predictive strength.

slides.title: HUI360: A 360° Egocentric Dataset and Baselines for Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation
slides.highlight: This work introduces HUI360, a large-scale egocentric dataset for anticipating human intentions, which supports the development of proactive and socially aware behavior in embodied agents relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: HUI360 is the largest in-the-wild 360° egocentric dataset for anticipating human-robot physical interactions.
card.key_idea: An automated pipeline using YOLOv11x, SAM2.1-L, and ViTPose/Sapiens to detect, track, and annotate physical interactions via segmentation mask intersection with robot interaction zones.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using RF, MLP, and LSTM baselines on AUC, F1, and AP across cross-dataset and cross-environment transfers; LSTM performed best.
card.limitation: Focuses only on physical contact, ignoring nuanced social cues like gaze, hesitation, or verbal engagement.

slides.title: How Should I Pick a Foundation Model for My Robot? In Favor of a Community Evaluation Framework for Social Robots
slides.tldr: EVALUATION FRAMEWORK FOR SOCIAL ROBOT FOUNDATION MODELS
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a three-tiered evaluation funnel to help select foundation models for social robots, focusing on dimensions like conversational competence and embodied character. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A proposed three-tiered evaluation funnel to help researchers select foundation models for social robots.
card.key_idea: Filters models through curated static benchmarks (T1), simulated interactions with LLM users/judges (T2), and robot-specific hardware evaluation (T3) across five social-interaction dimensions.
card.evaluation: Proposed as a framework; illustrated via a case study with the Haru robot. No quantitative results provided.
card.limitation: T3 remains robot-specific and costly; multimodal interaction and the boundary between simulation and live user studies are unresolved.

slides.title: Avalon-ToM-Bench: Evaluating Fine-Grained Theory of Mind via Asymmetric Game Mechanics
slides.tldr: NEW BENCHMARK FOR FINE-GRAINED THEORY OF MIND EVALUATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark to evaluate Theory of Mind (ToM) through asymmetric-information mechanics, finding that LLMs often represent correct mental states in hidden layers but fail to express them. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent via ToM.

card.one_liner: Avalon-ToM-Bench evaluates LLM Theory of Mind using asymmetric-information mechanics from the game The Resistance: Avalon.
card.key_idea: A 2x2 taxonomy (Epistemic vs. Motivational; Inference vs. Action) using perspective-constrained queries to decouple mental-state reasoning from general game-playing heuristics.
card.evaluation: 28 LLMs were tested on 408 binary items. Results show models represent correct mental states internally but fail to express them during generation.
card.limitation: Limited to a single game's mechanics, uses a binary verification format, and mechanistic steering was only tested on Qwen3 models.

slides.title: X2-Turn: Frame-Synchronous Dual-Head Modeling for Joint Streaming ASR and Turn State Prediction
slides.highlight: This work introduces X2-Turn, which jointly predicts ASR tokens and fine-grained turn states at the frame level to improve responsiveness in spoken dialogue systems. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement within human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: X2-Turn enables joint, frame-synchronous streaming ASR and turn state prediction using a dual-head architecture.
card.key_idea: Extends Voxtral Realtime with a parallel turn state head and ASR-anchored supervision, projecting word-level labels onto an 80ms frame-level timeline for simultaneous prediction.
card.evaluation: Tested on bilingual EasyTurn sets; outperformed SoulX-Duplug in accuracy and showed a controllable latency-accuracy trade-off via adjustable streaming delay $\tau$.
card.limitation: Joint training introduces a set-dependent degradation in ASR performance compared to ASR-only training.

slides.title: AI-Guided Learning: Research on Knowledge and Skill Acquisition Support Methods Using Deep Learning Audio-Video Processing Techniques
slides.tldr: AI-GUIDED LEARNING FRAMEWORK FOR SKILL ACQUISITION
slides.highlight: This research proposes a framework for content consumption and skill acquisition, including a system that learns proficiency from speech data to support pronunciation practice, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on estimating human proficiency and adaptive coaching.

card.one_liner: An AI-guided framework using deep learning to optimize audio-visual content consumption, comprehension, and skill imitation.
card.key_idea: Three systems: AIxSpeed (phoneme-level adaptive audio speed), FastPerson (multimodal video summarization with voice cloning), and Profy (model-derived feedback for pronunciation imitation).
card.evaluation: Evaluated via blind listening tests, quiz scores (40 participants), and expert pronunciation ratings; results showed 53% viewing time reduction and improved intelligibility.
card.limitation: Needs long-term effect validation and extension beyond audio-visual domains.

slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing and transferring contact-rich human bathing demonstrations to a soft robotic hand, contributing to the development of safe physical human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a robot-assisted system.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as a processing primitive to reconstruct synchronized motion, shape, and force, then retargets these to a soft robotic hand and arm.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world deployment on a mannequin using open- and closed-loop control.
card.limitation: Significant sim-to-real gap; closed-loop control uses aggregate pressure sums rather than distributions; not yet ready for human subjects.

slides.title: SAIN: Structure-Aware Interactive Navigation with Active Dialogue Grounding for Mobile Robot
slides.tldr: ZERO-SHOT INTERACTIVE NAVIGATION VIA DIALOGUE-TO-STATE CONVERSION
slides.highlight: This framework enables mobile robots to resolve ambiguous human instructions through active dialogue, converting oracle answers into persistent structured memory for navigation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: SAIN converts active dialogue into persistent structured memories for zero-shot interactive instance-goal navigation in robots.
card.key_idea: Dialogue answers are compiled into target evidence, route-level corridor memories, and object-candidate labels, which guide frontier ranking and target approach via a unified policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VL-LN IIGN benchmark; improved SR from 20.2 to 25.4 and SPL from 13.07 to 14.17 over the strongest dialogue-enabled baseline.

slides.title: DOBOT Unveils Humanoid Robot Designed for Life Beyond the Factory
slides.tldr: NEW HUMANOID ROBOT FOR NON-FACTORY USE
slides.highlight: DOBOT has introduced a humanoid robot intended for use outside of factory settings, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Toward Resilient Human-AI Collaboration: A Lifecycle Taxonomy of Sociotechnical Risks and Cascading Failures
slides.tldr: SOCIOTECHNICAL RISK TAXONOMY FOR HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: This paper identifies recurring risk clusters in human-AI collaboration, such as trust miscalibration and cognitive burden, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A lifecycle taxonomy of sociotechnical risks and cascading failures in human-AI collaboration across diverse professional domains.
card.key_idea: Proposes a four-stage lifecycle (task allocation, interaction, feedback, adoption) and six risk clusters to model how interconnected sociotechnical drivers cause systemic collaboration failures.
card.evaluation: Synthesized evidence from diverse application domains (healthcare, journalism, defense, etc.) and fragmented literature into a unified conceptual interaction model.
card.limitation: The paper provides a conceptual framework and synthesis for future empirical validation rather than presenting new experimental data.

slides.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation
slides.tldr: LEARNING HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOTION FROM HANDWRITING DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This research presents a framework for learning human-like robot motion using a dataset of handwriting demonstrations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework for learning human-like robot handwriting using an extended GMM+GMR approach and a new dataset.
card.key_idea: Extends GMM+GMR by incorporating contact force and normalized time dimensions and implementing segment-wise processing to handle non-continuous, multi-stroke trajectories from human demonstrations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a user study (21 participants) using a 0-100 human-likeness scale; generated trajectories scored 71.50, indicating perceived human-likeness.
card.limitation: Small participant sample sizes, lack of pen orientation data, and use of predefined guidelines that may limit generalizability.

slides.title: X Square Robot's HOST Learns from Short Videos
slides.highlight: X Square Robot's HOST demonstrates the ability to learn from short videos in 29 seconds, contributing to the field of embodied AI relevant to RwB.

slides.title: Vibe Compiler: A Research-Logic Synthesis Tool That Runs without Prompt Engineering
slides.highlight: This work proposes a Synthesis-Analysis Reciprocity Model and the Vibe Compiler to stimulate human metacognition, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and maintaining human-AI team alignment.

card.one_liner: Vibe Compiler transforms vague ideas into research logic by using AI to stimulate human metacognition.
card.key_idea: A Synthesis–Analysis Reciprocity Model where AI analyzes structural gaps in research logic and prompts users with reflective questions instead of providing answers.
card.evaluation: Prototype built on NotebookLM and Gemini; verified via execution logs for type-checking and logic construction. Quantitative effects on learners are not yet measured.
card.limitation: Requires the user to possess minimum domain knowledge and assumes AI can accurately compute objective structural indicators.

slides.title: From Speech to Interaction: Analyzing Multimodal Systems in Cocktail-Party Scenarios
slides.highlight: This work analyzes multimodal systems for recognizing speaker groups and transcribing conversations in cocktail-party scenarios, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Analysis of multimodal systems for cocktail-party speech recognition shows LLM-based semantic clustering and robust AVSR are most effective.
card.key_idea: Evaluates three strategies: audio-visual target speech separation, improved AVSR (e.g., AV-HuBERT, Whisper-Flamingo), and LLM-based semantic clustering for grouping speakers into conversations.
card.evaluation: Compared 12 systems on the CHiME-9 MCoRec dataset using WER, Clustering F1, and JointError; results show LLM-clustering is most robust.
card.limitation: Systems remain modular rather than end-to-end; semantic clustering depends on transcription quality, and visual cues generalize poorly.

slides.title: DuplexWorld: Can voice agents help you get through the day?
slides.highlight: This work introduces DuplexWorld to evaluate voice agents across diverse conversational scenarios and analytical capabilities, contributing to the understanding of conversational dialogue and turn-taking relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: DuplexWorld is a holistic benchmark evaluating voice agents across six diverse worlds and eleven conversation types.
card.key_idea: A unified evaluation suite measuring agentic capability (goal-state), conversational dynamics (turn-taking), and naturalness (DNSMOS) using simulated users across enterprise and navigation scenarios.
card.evaluation: Evaluated five commercial S2S systems across 156 scenarios. Results show a gap between conversational fluency and task completion (Pass@1: 0.490).
card.limitation: Does not use real human audio, relying instead on simulated users and a decision model for interruptions.

slides.title: I Gained Agency Over Agentic AI in a West 4th St Subway Station
slides.highlight: The text discusses user agency over agentic AI, which relates to ADAM-CHAT's focus on human-AI teaming and alignment with evolving team goals.

slides.title: The 'Rogue Model' storm: how to use agentic AI without losing control
slides.highlight: This discussion on maintaining control over agentic AI relates to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring, self-correction, and alignment within human-AI teams.

slides.title: Graphing the Everyday: A Neurosymbolic Approach to Eliciting Routines for Just-In-Time Adaptive Interventions
slides.tldr: NEUROSYMBOLIC ROUTINE ELICITATION FOR ADAPTIVE INTERVENTIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores a neurosymbolic pipeline combining LLMs and knowledge graphs to map human narratives into routines, which aligns with MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A neurosymbolic pipeline for eliciting user routines for health interventions reveals a gap between human narratives and AI extraction.
card.key_idea: Combines LLMs with a Neo4j knowledge graph to translate unstructured verbal narratives into structured schedule data for Just-In-Time Adaptive Interventions.
card.evaluation: Qualitative study with 16 participants using member-checking, state-machine diagrams, and knowledge graph traces to assess representational fidelity and human alignment.
card.limitation: Linear LLM extraction causes entity fragmentation and fails to capture non-linear, hierarchical storytelling and psychological receptivity.

slides.title: PromptShield Home: Ambient Multimodal Prompt Injection Defense for Smart-Home Agents
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL PROMPT INJECTION DEFENSE FOR SMART HOMES
slides.highlight: This work addresses addressee ambiguity and the ability of agents to distinguish genuine user commands from ambient content, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: PromptShield-Home benchmarks multimodal prompt injection in smart homes, finding MLLMs over-refuse while traditional detectors over-execute.
card.key_idea: A comparative framework testing three layers: traditional detectors (L0), single MLLM agents (L1), and multi-agent mediation (L2) across realistic ambient-signal scenarios.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 19 scenarios using unsafe-execution and safe-completion rates. Results show L0 and MLLMs have disjoint correct sets, reaching 94.1% via oracle.
card.limitation: Small benchmark size (N=19), reliance on an oracle rather than a trained router, and high VRAM requirements for the vision model.

slides.title: Certifying Collective Reasoning in Multi-Agent Systems via Koopman Spectral Analysis
slides.highlight: This work uses Koopman operator theory to provide certificates for convergence and reasoning dynamics in multi-agent systems, supporting the MOSAIC goal of aligning human-AI intent through a principled understanding of interaction dynamics.

card.one_liner: A Koopman operator framework that certifies convergence deadlines and reasoning factions in multi-agent LLM collectives.
card.key_idea: Treats collective reasoning as a nonlinear dynamical system, using Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) to linearize dynamics and derive certificates from the operator's spectrum.
card.evaluation: Tested on an attention-consensus model; spectral deadlines tracked observed convergence (r=0.93) and provided sound upper bounds in 96% of 24 configurations.
card.limitation: Validated primarily on a reference model; transfer to real LLM traces carries risks and requires further finite-sample theory.
